chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: concerning
A young boy who had not reached ten years of age committed zina with a woman. He عليه السلام said: “The boy is flogged with less than the hadd, and the woman is flogged with the full hadd.”

It was said to him: Then if she was muḥṣanah? He عليه السلام said: “She is not stoned, because the one who had intercourse with her is not legally mature; and if he had been legally mature, she would have been stoned.”

key_terms.مُحْصَنَةً: a married or otherwise legally protected woman subject to muḥṣan-related rulings

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on zina involving a boy who has not reached legal maturity?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning zina involving a minor boy who has not reached legal maturity. It distinguishes between the punishment of the non-mature boy and that of the woman, and it further clarifies that stoning does not apply to a muḥṣanah woman when the male partner is not legally mature.
